decision: First Sky School topic: why meteor showers appear to come from a radiant, using computed sky plus real Phaethon radar imagery
rationale: The payoff is the computation itself: parallel debris paths plus our head-on view explain the illusion, and the sky renderer can show meteors diverging from the radiant. The real Arecibo radar image of Phaethon is the one piece of imagery that carries the 'asteroid, not comet' point without an artist's impression. Every number (73 deg, 150/h) is computed or sourced.
alternatives: Do the topic as a Moon-distance explainer (rejected: orbit3d draws planets only, so the geometry could not be shown truthfully)
Use an artist's impression of Phaethon (rejected: not real imagery)
